title: K-flat line tensor models and finite balancing
statement: Let l be prime, E/Q_l a finite extension, and X a scheme. Write R for the completed integral coefficient sheaf and R_n for its positive-power finite quotients. For every rank-one finite locally free R-module sheaf T and every flat-term K-flat complex P, T[0] is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex] and Tot(P tensor_R T[0]) is a flat-term K-flat complex [def-pur-integral-derived-operations, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. For each n, extension of scalars from R to R_n gives an isomorphism R_n tensor_R Tot(P tensor_R T[0]) to Tot((R_n tensor_R P) tensor_{R_n} (R_n tensor_R T[0])). On the summand in bidegree (p,q) it sends a tensor (x tensor y) to (a tensor x) tensor (1 tensor y).

proof.text: Apply line_unbounded_derived_tensor to the actual completed integral coefficient ring and the given rank-one locally free T. Retain its K-flatness of T[0] and its termwise flatness. Apply kFlat_total_tensor_model to P and T[0], using P.property for the two hypotheses on P. Its first two clauses are precisely Good for integralLineComplex.

Apply the proved scalarTensorTotal helper of IntegralTensorReductionTowerComparison to the actual finite reduction functor, using its prescribed object and map equations. Evaluate its natural chain isomorphism at (P,T[0]). Its scalar-one generator equation is definitionally the equation for IntegralOnSlice.generator, because both use toSheafify and the same object equality. Substitute k=p+q. For an arbitrary finite coefficient a, express generator(a,x) as a times generator(1,x), using the scalar-extension tensor action and linearity of sheafification and the object-equality cast. Every component of the comparison is linear. The total tensor generator is linear in its first factor, by TensorProduct.smul_tmul and linearity of the sheafification unit and summand inclusion. These identities multiply the scalar-one equation by a and give exactly the required generator formula. No flatness of the quotient map, boundedness of P, or nonzero coefficient hypothesis is introduced.
